priority_scale.Critical: Required for the system to be viable or safe.
priority_scale.High: Important for the primary workflow; omission causes major impact.
priority_scale.Medium: Valuable requirement that can follow the primary workflow.
priority_scale.Low: Useful enhancement with limited impact if deferred.

requirements.name: Management reporting scope
requirements.explanation: Provide management-process reports and analysis tools for library managers, administrators, and staff, without reducing or replacing the day-to-day patron-facing OPAC and circulation functionality.

requirements.name: Collection-use analysis
requirements.explanation: Provide analysis of the library collection and how it is used by patrons, including output formats suitable for management review and actionable drill-down where applicable.

requirements.name: Branch-capacity analysis
requirements.explanation: Provide analysis of branch capacity and support decisions for optimal distribution of the collection across branches.

requirements.name: Patron-demographics and interests analysis
requirements.explanation: Provide analysis of patron demographics and interests to support planning and management decisions (define required outputs, granularity, time window(s), refresh frequency, and success criteria in implementation).

requirements.name: Staff productivity and workflow analysis
requirements.explanation: Provide analysis of staff productivity and workflow to help identify process bottlenecks and performance improvements (define required outputs, measurement approach, time windows, and success criteria in implementation).

requirements.name: Financial-transaction tracking
requirements.explanation: Support tracking and verification of financial transactions and provide auditability and reconciliation support (implementation must specify audit trail format, retention, encryption, access controls, and reconciliation procedures).

requirements.name: Executive reports interface
requirements.explanation: Provide an Executive Reports Interface with the predefined set of reports needed by library executives and directors, including role-based access to report sets and required metadata (owner, parameters, run time, etc.).

requirements.name: Library report templates
requirements.explanation: Provide report templates needed by all PINES libraries and support template management (including parameterization and template distribution via configuration migration).

requirements.name: Data-quality reports
requirements.explanation: Provide reports that identify data-quality issues, enabling staff to detect, diagnose, and correct quality problems (define measurable outputs and coverage).

requirements.name: Inventory reports
requirements.explanation: Provide inventory reports for operational and management oversight (define inventory scope, refresh cadence, and output formats).

requirements.name: Capacity reports
requirements.explanation: Provide capacity reports for branch capacity management (define capacity metrics, time windows, and performance expectations).

requirements.name: Cross-branch comparison reports
requirements.explanation: Provide reports that compare data across library branches, supporting consistent metrics and drill-down for analysis (define comparison dimensions and normalization rules).

requirements.name: In-transit item reports
requirements.explanation: Provide reports on in-transit items to support delivery coordination (define item identifiers, shipment status derivation, and update frequency).

requirements.name: Missing and damaged item reports
requirements.explanation: Provide missing-item and damaged-item reports that can be produced per branch (define report filters, statuses, and data refresh behavior).

requirements.name: Weeding support reports
requirements.explanation: Provide reports to support collection weeding decisions (define inputs, time windows, and the measurable outputs required to justify weeding).

requirements.name: Shelf-space utilization reports
requirements.explanation: Provide reports on shelf-space utilization (define granularity such as branch/floor/shelf/category and data sources for utilization).

requirements.name: Program-planning demographics
requirements.explanation: Provide demographic analysis capabilities to support library program planning (define required outputs, time windows, and update/refresh frequency).

requirements.name: Report queue visibility
requirements.explanation: Allow users to view the status and contents of the report-processing queue, with sufficient metadata to diagnose delays or failures (define authorization rules, queue ownership, and metadata fields).

requirements.name: Non-disruptive report processing
requirements.explanation: Report processing must not disrupt other system functions during open hours, including the circulation client; implement quantitative constraints and operational isolation such as acceptable latency/queue wait times and max resource impact during peak usage (define SLAs in implementation).

requirements.name: Background/queued report processing
requirements.explanation: Generate reports using background processing and/or queuing so that report generation does not slow the circulation client during peak hours; implementation must include concrete architecture and performance constraints (choose one or more approaches and specify SLAs).

requirements.name: Consortium scale capacity support
requirements.explanation: Support a consortium with 286 locations and ~17 million annual circulations, including purchasing and processing of >900,000 items per year; define measurable performance/capacity targets (concurrent users, peak-hour transactions, throughput, indexing/update rates) tied to these numbers and test scenarios.

requirements.name: Relational database backend compatible with Evergreen
requirements.explanation: Use a fully relational database backend that operates properly with the Evergreen relational data structure; implementation must specify Evergreen version expectations, schema compatibility, migrations, and verification tests (export/import formats and compatibility testing).

requirements.name: Enterprise ILS integration
requirements.explanation: Integrate with an enterprise-level library automation system (including Acquisitions and Cataloging) and rely on its data structures and functionality.

requirements.name: OPAC and patron data access
requirements.explanation: Interact with the OPAC and patron data, including holds and circulation data created through the patron interface; define the authorized data sources and read/write scope for management reporting.

requirements.name: Vendor data integration
requirements.explanation: Provide interfaces to vendor websites through published APIs and/or automated transfers of standard-format data files including USMARC21 and EDIFACT; implementation must specify authentication, exchange formats, frequencies, error-handling, and reconciliation procedures.

requirements.name: Configuration migration across environments
requirements.explanation: Provide separate development and training environments and support migrating report templates and configurations from those environments to production.

requirements.name: Online help system
requirements.explanation: Provide hierarchical, cross-linked online HTML help that is descriptive and illustrative of all system functions; implementation must specify coverage mapping and whether context-sensitive help is required per-screen or per-field.

requirements.name: Error reporting and feedback
requirements.explanation: Provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback for management-process operations.

requirements.name: Administrator query feedback
requirements.explanation: Provide low-level, query-specific feedback for Local System Administrators and Global System Administrators in the front-end interface.

requirements.name: Centralized multi-location operation
requirements.explanation: Operate from a central location while accepting input from and providing services to multiple library locations.

requirements.name: Process documentation (developer deliverables)
requirements.explanation: Provide a thorough high-level description of major processes, including bibliographic-record import/export, validation against internal/external authority sources, and standard reports.

requirements.name: Data specifications (developer deliverables)
requirements.explanation: Provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the management processes.

requirements.name: Standards-compliant HTML outputs
requirements.explanation: Ensure produced HTML for report displays, help content, and web-based UI components is valid and standards-compliant; implementation must specify applicable standards/validation tooling and pass criteria.

requirements.name: Assistive technology compatibility
requirements.explanation: The system shall be usable with screen readers, screen magnification, and other assistive software including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText (implementation must also map to a concrete accessibility conformance standard and test method if required).

requirements.name: Staff report authoring/contribution
requirements.explanation: Allow staff to create or contribute report content and report definitions; implementation must define the authoring interface, permission model, and what can/cannot be edited.

requirements.name: OPAC isolation from management-process constraints
requirements.explanation: The management-process system must not constrain or reduce OPAC functionality or features.

requirements.name: Flexible role-based access control
requirements.explanation: Control user rights and privileges using security groups and/or roles; implementation must define permission granularity, whether both are used, and role-to-permission mappings for reports, queues, and administrative functions.

requirements.name: Access via supported client types
requirements.explanation: Provide access through a web browser and/or a Windows-compatible client; implementation must clarify whether either is sufficient or whether both are mandatory and specify supported browser/app versions and deprecation policy.

blacklist.reason: Conflicting status resolved: this candidate is kept and merged as a primary access-control requirement with clarified implementation expectations; therefore it is not discarded.

Discarded due to missing specificity: card technology (e.g., HID), reader/authentication mechanism, mapping to identities/roles, and whether it applies to this reporting system versus broader authentication. Not enough technical detail to be enforceable.

blacklist.statement: Server operating systems (Linux or Solaris servers)
blacklist.reason: Discarded due to platform version/support-boundary ambiguity. While operating platform constraints matter, the requirement as stated is not enforceable without supported versions and a support/deprecation policy. Replaced by database/architecture and performance requirements where applicable.

Discarded because the specified browser versions are obsolete and conflict with modern security/platform expectations; would likely prevent secure operation. Kept as a general client-access requirement only (without obsolete version constraints).

Discarded as written because the applicable Section 508 revision/version and measurable conformance/testing criteria were not defined. Accessibility is retained via assistive-technology compatibility, but a concrete standard must be specified separately if required.

blacklist.statement: Background vs non-disruptive report processing as alternatives
blacklist.reason: Not discarded as a whole: non-disruptive report processing and background/queued processing are kept separately but with clarified requirement to define quantitative SLAs/constraints. The prior concern was about implementation choice ambiguity, addressed in kept requirements.

Discarded as a standalone requirement because it lacks required granularity definition (per-screen/per-field/context mapping) and maintenance expectations. Context-sensitive help may be implemented, but it must be specified to be enforceable; the broader online help system is kept.

blacklist.statement: Report development testing gate (Reports Working Group review before release)
blacklist.reason: Discarded because it is an organizational development-process control rather than a runtime software requirement; not appropriate for a software requirements document without converting into a specific, testable delivery criterion.
